issues.title: Missing private modifier on gleanWrapper
issues.description: The rule requires that properties have explicit access control modifiers with 'private' for implementation details. The gleanWrapper property lacks the 'private' modifier, exposing an internal implementation detail that should not be accessible outside the struct.
issues.rule_name: Properties and Methods Must Have Appropriate Access Control

issues.title: Incorrect Reader Mode URL handling in cancelEditMode
issues.description: The cancelEditMode function now incorrectly preserves reader mode URLs when canceling edit mode. The logic was changed from '&&' (AND) to '||' (OR), which means reader mode URLs will now be kept instead of being cleared. This breaks the expected behavior where reader mode URLs should be filtered out when canceling URL editing, potentially causing the address bar to display internal reader:// URLs to users instead of the original webpage URL.

issues.title: Inverted reader mode telemetry state tracking
issues.description: The recordReaderModeTelemetry function has inverted logic for determining reader mode state. When the reader mode is 'available' (about to be enabled), it reports false instead of true, and for all other states it reports true instead of false. This causes telemetry data to incorrectly track reader mode usage patterns - reporting that reader mode is being disabled when it's actually being enabled and vice versa. This will corrupt analytics data about reader mode feature usage.

issues.title: Wrong display view type for reader mode action
issues.description: The handleShowReaderModeAction function sets the wrong displayView type when the user taps the reader mode button. Instead of setting displayView to '.readerMode' (which would show the reader mode view), it's set to '.readerModeLongPressAction' (which is meant for long-press actions). This causes the wrong UI component to be displayed when users try to activate reader mode, breaking the core reader mode functionality and showing an incorrect action sheet instead of the reader view.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #31577 - Remove FXIOS-14593 [BVC] Clean up qr code related code from BVC

structured_output.summary:
The PR removes the QR-code scanner entry point from the browser toolbar and quick actions: the `QRCodeViewControllerDelegate` conformance on BrowserViewController, the `showQRCode`/`handleQRCode` paths, the `.qrCode` toolbar action, the `QRCode` shortcut/deeplink/route, the QR telemetry events, and the corresponding tests and mocks. The deletions are mostly clean. My grep of the Swift sources and tests found no remaining references to the removed symbols, and the QR scanner itself is still reachable from Settings, Remote Tabs and FxA.

The PR also carries several changes that have nothing to do with QR cleanup, and two of them are real defects. First, `BrowserViewControllerState.handleShowReaderModeAction` now maps to `.readerModeLongPressAction` instead of `.readerMode`. The toolbar's reader-mode button dispatches `showReaderMode`, so tapping it now runs `toggleReaderModeLongPressAction()`, which adds the page to the reading list instead of toggling reader mode. Second, the reader-mode telemetry `isEnabled` ternary is inverted against its own comment, and the existing test asserting `enabled == false` should now fail. The PR also changes the `cancelEditMode` URL filter from `&&` to `||` and bumps the app version, neither of which is explained.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The reader-mode display-state swap silently changes the toolbar reader-mode button from toggling reader mode to adding the page to the reading list. That is a user-visible regression in core browsing functionality and is not covered by any test. The inverted telemetry flag breaks an existing assertion. The cancelEditMode logic change and the version bump are unrelated to the stated scope and need either a revert or a justification. The QR removal itself is sound once these are addressed.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, the browser toolbar's QR button and the home-screen QR quick action both reached the QR scanner through BrowserViewController. The toolbar path went ToolbarMiddleware, which dispatched GeneralBrowserAction.showQRcodeReader, then BVC's handleDisplayActions, which called navigationHandler.showQRCode, then BrowserCoordinator, QRCodeCoordinator and QRCodeViewController. The quick action path went QuickActions, then RouteBuilder, then Route.AppAction.showQRCode, then BrowserCoordinator.handleQRCode. Scan results came back to BVC through QRCodeViewControllerDelegate and were turned into navigation or telemetry.

This PR cuts both entry points. The toolbar action, display state, delegate conformance, route, shortcut type, deeplink input, and Glean metrics are all deleted. The QRCodeCoordinator and QRCodeViewController stay in place because Settings, Remote Tabs, Bookmarks and FxA still use them. The PR also changes reader-mode handling in the same files: the display-state mapping for showReaderMode and the telemetry and cancel-edit logic in ToolbarMiddleware.
steps: Start at the toolbar boundary: ToolbarMiddleware receives toolbar taps and dispatches GeneralBrowserAction. The `.qrCode` case is removed, and the `.readerMode` case still dispatches `showReaderMode`.

BrowserViewControllerState maps GeneralBrowserActionType values to DisplayType. The `showQRcodeReader` → `.qrCodeReader` mapping is removed. The `showReaderMode` mapping is also changed from `.readerMode` to `.readerModeLongPressAction`, and that change is the regression to review.

BrowserViewController.handleDisplayActions consumes DisplayType. It no longer presents the QR reader, and `.readerMode` now has no producer while `.readerModeLongPressAction` handles the reader-mode toolbar tap.

The quick-action path is removed upstream: ShortcutType, DeeplinkInput.AppAction, Route.AppAction, and RouteBuilder no longer produce `showQRCode`, and BrowserCoordinator no longer forwards it to BVC.

Telemetry is trimmed: ToolbarTelemetry drops qrCodeButtonTapped, TelemetryWrapper drops qrCodeText/qrCodeURL, and metrics.yaml drops the qr_code and qr_scan_button_tapped probes. The reader-mode telemetry in ToolbarMiddleware is also altered in this PR.
Tests and mocks are updated to match the removed surface. The test suite does not cover the reader-mode display-state mapping, which is how the regression above can slip through.

findings.title: Toolbar reader-mode button now adds to reading list instead of toggling reader mode
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Browser/BrowserViewController/State/BrowserViewControllerState.swift`, `handleShowReaderModeAction` (around line 566) now sets `displayView: .readerModeLongPressAction`. Revert it to `.readerMode`, so the toolbar reader-mode button calls `toggleReaderMode()` again instead of `toggleReaderModeLongPressAction()`, which adds the page to the reading list. Leave `handleAddToReadingListLongPressAction` (around line 590) unchanged. Then add a unit test in the BrowserViewControllerState test suite that dispatches `GeneralBrowserActionType.showReaderMode` and asserts `displayView == .readerMode`.

findings.title: Reader-mode telemetry `enabled` flag is inverted, breaking an existing test
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Browser/Toolbars/Redux/ToolbarMiddleware.swift`, `recordReaderModeTelemetry` (lines 523-526) has the `isEnabled` switch inverted: `.available` returns `false` while the comment says the mode will be enabled after the action, so it should be `true`. Restore the original mapping: `.available` → `true`, `default` → `false`. Confirm that `testDidTapButton_tapOnReaderModeButton_dispatchesShowReaderModes` in `ToolbarMiddlewareTests.swift` still passes, and do not edit its expectations.

findings.title: Unrelated change to cancelEditMode URL filter
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Browser/Toolbars/Redux/ToolbarMiddleware.swift`, `cancelEditMode(windowUUID:)` (around line 485) changed the URL filter from `isWebPage() && !isReaderModeURL` to `isWebPage() || isReaderModeURL`. This is unrelated to removing the QR code and is not described in the PR. Revert it to the original `&&` / `!isReaderModeURL` condition unless the author can justify it, in which case split it into a separate PR with a test that covers reader-mode URLs on cancel edit.

findings.title: Unrelated app version bump in version.xcconfig
findings.body:
`APP_VERSION` is bumped from 147.1 to 147.2. A QR-code cleanup should not change the release version. This is usually done by the release process, and a feature PR bumping it can conflict with release branches and make the version history harder to read.

::diff{file="firefox-ios/Client/Configuration/version.xcconfig" lines="1-1"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Configuration/version.xcconfig`, `APP_VERSION` was bumped from 147.1 to 147.2 in a QR-code cleanup PR. Revert the line to `APP_VERSION = 147.1` unless the release process requires this bump in this PR.

findings.title: Dead `BrowserCoordinator.showQRCode` left behind
findings.body:
After this PR, BVC no longer calls `navigationHandler?.showQRCode(delegate:)`. The toolbar path is the only caller of `BrowserCoordinator.showQRCode(delegate:rootNavigationController:)` that the removed code used. It is now only exercised by `BrowserCoordinatorTests` lines 418-428. The method may still be needed to satisfy the navigation-handler protocol, which I did not verify. If it is not required, it is dead code that the PR's own goal should remove.

::code{file="firefox-ios/Client/Coordinators/Browser/BrowserCoordinator.swift" lines="953-974"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Coordinators/Browser/BrowserCoordinator.swift`, `showQRCode(delegate:rootNavigationController:)` (around lines 953-974) is no longer called from production code after BVC dropped the toolbar QR path. Check whether the navigation-handler protocol that `BrowserCoordinator` conforms to still requires it. If it does not, remove the method, and update the tests in `BrowserCoordinatorTests.swift` (around lines 418-428) that call it. If it does, leave it and note why in the PR.

findings.title: Unused visibility widening on ToolbarTelemetry.gleanWrapper
findings.body:
`ToolbarTelemetry.gleanWrapper` changed from `private let` to `let`, which widens access to the module. Nothing in the diff or the repo reads `toolbarTelemetry.gleanWrapper`, and the QR telemetry that might have needed it is removed. The change is unexplained and leaks an implementation detail.

::diff{file="firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Browser/Toolbars/ToolbarTelemetry.swift" lines="8-12"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Browser/Toolbars/ToolbarTelemetry.swift`, `gleanWrapper` (line 9) was changed from `private let` to `let`. No caller uses it. Restore `private let gleanWrapper: GleanWrapper` unless a caller that needs the wider access is added in this PR.

findings.title: QR removal is clean across Swift sources and tests
findings.body: The removed symbols (`.qrCode` toolbar action, `showQRcodeReader`, `qrCodeReader` display type, `ShortcutType.qrCode`, `AppAction.showQRCode`, the `QRCodeViewControllerDelegate` conformance, and the `qrCodeText`/`qrCodeURL` telemetry) have no remaining references in Swift sources or tests. The QRCodeCoordinator, QRCodeViewController and the Settings, Remote Tabs, Bookmarks and FxA entry points are left intact, so the scanner still works where it is used elsewhere. The PR also removes the matching tests and mocks and the `handleQRCode` override, so the build should stay consistent.
